main_issue: Only the Snowflake case establishes a concrete missing-redaction mechanism: DEBUG logging of a command response that carries encryption material. The Para case supplies only a narrow source anchor with no description, trace, source-to-sink path, or fix evidence, so it cannot yet be shown to share that mechanism. The current guideline also expands improperly into generic validation, authorization, isolation, and state-check failures.
split_suggestions: Sensitive values contained in structured command, API, or storage responses are emitted to logs or exception messages before field-level redaction.
Separate any confirmed log-forging or log-injection cases from confidential-data disclosure; attacker-controlled log formatting is a different source, exploit condition, and fix.
evidence_notes: snowflakedb__snowflake-jdbc::CVE-2025-27496: parseCommandInGS logs the complete GS JsonNode at DEBUG level; the same response drives encryption-material extraction, establishing a sensitive-response-to-log sink path without prior masking.
erudika__para::CVE-2025-48955: HealthUtils.java:132-134 alone is insufficient to identify the logged/thrown value, its sensitivity, its attacker influence, or the missing redaction guard.
The cluster summary mentions both sensitive-data disclosure and log injection, but these are not demonstrated as one reusable mechanism by the supplied evidence.

The proposed query is effectively mechanism-agnostic because it searches for arbitrary missing validation/authorization/isolation guards rather than structured sensitive data reaching a logging or exception sink.
